entries.name: length
entries.notes: Alias of size.

entries.name: push
entries.notes: Converts through the element boundary.

entries.name: pop
entries.notes: Removes the last element; empty array raises.

entries.name: front
entries.notes: Empty array raises. An object, array or map element comes back as a reference to it, like a C++ reference return: binding the result to var, auto or T copies the element, while var&, T& and a member call on the result reach the stored element.

entries.name: back
entries.notes: Empty array raises. An object, array or map element comes back as a reference to it, like a C++ reference return: binding the result to var, auto or T copies the element, while var&, T& and a member call on the result reach the stored element.

entries.name: first
entries.notes: Alias of front. An object, array or map element comes back as a reference to it, like a C++ reference return: binding the result to var, auto or T copies the element, while var&, T& and a member call on the result reach the stored element.

entries.name: last
entries.notes: Alias of back. An object, array or map element comes back as a reference to it, like a C++ reference return: binding the result to var, auto or T copies the element, while var&, T& and a member call on the result reach the stored element.

entries.name: index_of
entries.notes: Language equality; -1 if absent.

entries.name: has
entries.notes: Language equality.

entries.name: contains
entries.notes: Alias of has.

entries.name: slice
entries.signature: slice(start: int = 0, end: int = size()) -> array<T>
entries.notes: Retains the selected range in place, end exclusive; defaults 0 and size, negative indices relative to end, bounds clamp. Retained elements move without cloning. Returns the receiver; array::slice returns a copy.
entries.display: array<T>.slice(start: int = 0, end: int = size()) -> array<T>

entries.name: filter
entries.notes: Filters in place, retaining element constraints and selected values without cloning. Reference callback parameters target live elements. Returns the receiver; array::filter returns a copy.

entries.name: sort
entries.signature: sort(predicate: function(T, T) -> bool = omitted) -> void
entries.notes: Mutates in place; optional bool predicate, otherwise language <, with <=> fallback for class and builtin orders. Errors stop sorting without committing the order; callback side effects remain. Strict weak ordering required. Typed primitive buffers avoid boxing. Default numeric sorting treats signed zeros as equivalent and groups all NaNs last; an explicit predicate supplies its own order.
entries.display: array<T>.sort(predicate: function(T, T) -> bool = omitted) -> void

entries.name: remove
entries.notes: Removes by index; false without change when out of range.

entries.name: remove_if
entries.notes: Removes matches; returns removed count.

entries.name: join
entries.notes: Stringifies values between separators.

entries.name: map
entries.notes: Maps in place, retaining input element constraints; results convert through the usual typed-element rules. Reference callback parameters target live elements. Returns the receiver; array::map can change result type.

entries.name: reduce
entries.signature: reduce(callback: function(var, T[, int]) -> R, initial: var = first_element) -> R
entries.notes: Without initial, empty array raises; callback receives accumulator and element, optionally index. The accumulator starts as a copy of the initial value (or of the first element), as std::accumulate takes its init by value.
entries.display: array<T>.reduce(callback: function(var, T[, int]) -> R, initial: var = first_element) -> R

example.code:
array<int> xs = [1, 2, 3, 4];
print(xs.reduce((sum, x) => sum + x), " ", xs.reduce((sum, x) => sum + x, 100));

entries.name: for_each
entries.notes: T& callback parameters bind live elements.

example.code:
array<string> xs = ["a", "b"];
xs.for_each((s, i) => print(i, ": ", s));

entries.name: find
entries.signature: find(predicate: function(T[, int]) -> bool) -> T or null
entries.notes: First match, copied; null if absent. Value results copy, while shared_ptr/weak_ptr handles retain identity.
entries.display: array<T>.find(predicate: function(T[, int]) -> bool) -> T or null

example.code:
array<string> names = ["ann", "bob", "cy"];
print(names.find(n => n.size() == 3), " ", names.find(n => n == "zed"));

entries.name: find_index
entries.notes: First match index; -1 if absent.

example.code:
array<string> names = ["ann", "bob", "cy"];
print(names.find_index(n => n == "cy"), " ", names.find_index(n => n == "zed"));

entries.name: some
entries.notes: True if any match; short circuits.

example.code:
array<int> xs = [1, 3, 4];
print(xs.some(x => x % 2 == 0), " ", xs.every(x => x > 0));

entries.name: every
entries.notes: True if all match; empty array is true.

entries.name: concat
entries.notes: Appends the other array in place, retaining input element constraints. Same-kind primitive/string/vector buffers avoid per-element boxing. Added values copy; handles share. Returns the receiver; alias of append.

entries.name: insert
entries.notes: Index from 0 through size inclusive.

entries.name: length
entries.notes: Alias of size.

entries.name: contains
entries.notes: Keys never coerce.

entries.name: has
entries.notes: Alias of contains.

entries.name: erase
entries.notes: Alias of remove(key); true if an entry was removed, false when absent.

example.code:
map<string, int> stock = {"axe": 2, "bow": 1};
print(stock.erase("axe"), " ", stock.erase("axe"), " ", to_json(stock));

entries.name: remove
entries.notes: True if an entry was removed; false when absent.

entries.name: keys
entries.notes: Key order; keys become detached values. Value results copy, while shared_ptr/weak_ptr handles retain identity.

entries.name: values
entries.notes: Values in key order. Value results copy, while shared_ptr/weak_ptr handles retain identity.

entries.name: get
entries.signature: get(key: K, fallback: var = null) -> V or var
entries.notes: Does not insert; returns the stored value or fallback; missing keys default to null. An object, array or map element comes back as a reference to it, like a C++ reference return: binding the result to var, auto or T copies the element, while var&, T& and a member call on the result reach the stored element.
entries.display: map<K,V>.get(key: K, fallback: var = null) -> V or var

example.code:
map<string, int> stock = {"axe": 2};
print(stock.get("axe"), " ", stock.get("bow"), " ", stock.get("bow", 0), " ", stock.size());

entries.name: to_array
entries.notes: Ordered [key,value] arrays; not Pair objects. Value results copy, while shared_ptr/weak_ptr handles retain identity.

entries.name: filter
entries.notes: Keeps the entries the predicate accepts in place, retaining key/value constraints, and returns the receiver; map::filter returns a copy. Callback value references target live entries.

entries.name: filter
entries.signature: filter(values: map<K,V>, predicate: function(K, V) -> bool) -> map<K,V>
entries.notes: Returns a new map of the entries the predicate accepts, preserving key/value constraints; the input does not mutate. Only selected value elements copy; explicit handles retain identity.
entries.display: map::filter(values: map<K,V>, predicate: function(K, V) -> bool) -> map<K,V>

entries.name: remove_if
entries.notes: Returns removed count; keys remain immutable.

example.code:
map<string, int> stock = {"axe": 2, "bow": 0, "cap": 0};
print(stock.remove_if((k, v) => v == 0), " ", to_json(stock));
